transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM), Maya (Sierra Head ML Ops), Jon (CTO), Evan (Sr Data Eng)

Summary: Quarterly health check / QBR focusing on usage trends, cost optimization opportunities, stability/incident review, and roadmap alignment. Customer is evaluating moving part of batch inference to Dedicated and wants deeper security review for Private deployment later this year.

Topics: usage, cost, latency p95, dedicated vs hosted, private deployment considerations (VPC/KMS), upcoming model rollouts, action items and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Um, this is Alex from Redwood, with Priya and Jordan. How's it going at Sierra?
[00:07] Maya: Hey Alex, hey team. Busy, but good. Thanks for doing the QBR.
[00:11] Jon: Afternoon. We wanted to cover a few items — usage spike last month, cost budget pressure, and also privacy questions for our next fiscal quarter.
[00:20] Alex: Totally, that's the plan. We'll run through the metrics, some recommendations from Redwood Optimize, and then Priya will go over performance and Dedicated options.
[00:29] Priya: Hi all. Quick note: apologies in advance for background noise, I'm on commuter train.
[00:34] Evan: No worries.

[00:36] Alex: Alright first slide — usage. We saw from your account telemetry that tokens consumed up ~42% QoQ, mostly from the customer support summarization flows and an internal vector search re-rank. Maya, is that aligned with what you saw?
[00:49] Maya: Yeah that's right. We onboarded a new support channel in February and it's heavier than expected; long conversations mean bigger contexts. The median seq length jumped from 600 to about 1,100 tokens.
[01:02] Priya: That explains the p95 latency bump; the runtime kernel selection is running more long-context paths. We've got a few knobs — batching and prefix cache — that can help, but it's a tradeoff with tail latency.
[01:15] Jon: Can you remind us on the KV cache behavior? We noticed the docs mention KV cache but not sure how it applies to our multi-tenant setup.
[01:22] Priya: Sure, so KV cache is per-hosted session for generation workloads, it avoids recomputing prefix attention. In your current hosted setup we can enable more aggressive prefix caching for the support flow — it saves compute but requires consistent routing to the same backend to reclaim the cache. With Dedicated you'd get more deterministic cache residency.
[01:38] Evan: Any gotchas with cache invalidation? We have ephemeral contexts for privacy reasons.
[01:43] Priya: Good question — if you purge conversation state we evict the cache, obviously. For privacy constraints you can use shorter retention or per-customer namespaces; that still improves hit rate for repeated queries. There was a small timing hiccup in one of your requests last month where the cache warming caused a 200–300 ms transient.
[01:59] Maya: Yep we saw that on 2026-03-14 during the incident. Can you walk through the root cause again?
[02:05] Alex: Jordan, do you want me to pull up the incident notes? But the short version: there was an autoscaler edge case with burst traffic hitting a cold host, plus concurrent quantization fallbacks which increased scheduling jitter. We rolled a patch in the runtime to reduce cold-start windows.
[02:21] Jordan: The fix helped; our errors dropped. But from a SLO perspective, our internal target is p95 < 400ms for customer-facing flows and that was briefly violated.
[02:33] Priya: Right. For the next quarter we recommend two things: 1) Dedicated pool for the support flows to reduce variability, and 2) continued use of prefix caching + smaller batching window to keep p95 predictable.
[02:46] Jon: What is the approximate cost delta if we move the support flows (about 35% of tokens) to Dedicated?
[02:53] Alex: Quick back-of-envelope: with your current usage, a reserved Dedicated pool sized to your sustained throughput plus 20% headroom versus hosted on-demand would lower per-token compute cost by approx 18–28%, depending on utilization. We'll send a detailed pricing model.
[03:07] Maya: We need concrete numbers, with scenarios for 60/70/80% utilization.
[03:11] Alex: Absolutely — action item for me to send the pricing sheet with three utilization scenarios.

[03:18] Evan: On the topic of quantization — the team saw some regression in a few prompts after you rolled the 4-bit quantized variant in March. Any notes?
[03:26] Priya: There were a couple of edge prompts where the 4-bit QAT path produced slightly different tokenization, especially with long code blocks. We recommend running a small eval set as part of the rollout; Redwood Optimize can suggest which prompts are most sensitive.
[03:40] Maya: Can Redwood run that eval on our staging corpus? We can share a masked dataset.
[03:45] Priya: Yes we can — we'll need a staging key or we can run on your Dedicated environment if you prefer. Either way, we can do a controlled A/B with canary rollouts.

[03:55] Jon: Security — big item. We're evaluating a Private deployment (VPC + KMS) for regulated customers. What does Redwood support for key management and audit logs?
[04:04] Alex: For Private we support customer-managed KMS + HSM integrations. Audit logs are available via Console and can be pushed to your SIEM; we also provide detailed model-level access logs.
[04:13] Jordan: We've already got your SOC 2 report but need more details on key rotation and encryption at rest. I'll send the auditor questions.
[04:20] Alex: Great — Jordan, we'll line up a security deep-dive. Priya, can you own the technical portion?
[04:25] Priya: Yep I'll coordinate.

[04:28] Maya: Also data residency — some EMEA customers want EU data residency. Is there a plan to regionally pin data?
[04:34] Alex: Yes, we have EU regions available for Hosted and Private; for Dedicated you can pin capacity in our EU cluster for guaranteed residency. We'll include region-specific pricing in the sheet.
[04:44] Jon: Thanks. On reliability, are there any recommended changes to our alerting? We use Prometheus + PagerDuty.
[04:50] Priya: The Console exposes token-level latency and error rate alerts; we can push metrics to your Prometheus endpoint or via a push gateway. Recommend threshold-based alerts on p95 and on error-rate per route. Also set a fallback policy that routes to a lower-cost model in case of sustained errors.
[05:07] Evan: If we route to a fallback model, will the output quality drop dramatically? Our customers care about answer fidelity.
[05:12] Priya: It depends on the route. For re-rank tasks you can often use a smaller model with similar quality; for multi-turn summarization it's riskier. We can define per-route fallback policies using Redwood Console.

[05:24] Alex: Quick note about billing anomalies — you had two days in March where usage spiked due to a runaway job. We suggested quota guards and a per-route daily cap. Have you enabled those?
[05:34] Maya: We turned on the per-route soft caps but didn't set hard limits yet — worried about breaking production.
[05:40] Alex: Start with a soft cap with email alerts, then a hard cap during off-hours if you need. Also consider request-level budget tokens the SDK exposes.

[05:52] Jon: Roadmap alignment — we're interested in ingest-time embeddings for search and lower-cost vector store offloads. Any roadmap items from Redwood that help?
[05:59] Priya: We're shipping an embeddings caching layer and a cheaper low-precision embedding model this quarter. That should drop embedding costs for cold storage and retrieval. We'll give you early access to the beta.
[06:10] Maya: Excellent. Can we get an ETA?
[06:12] Priya: Beta next month, GA in about 2 months pending internal validation.

[06:17] Evan: A quick note — we ran a PoC with Anthropic for a month. Costs were similar but tooling and observability were better at Redwood — your Console traces were helpful.
[06:28] Alex: Appreciate that. We do get compared to OpenAI too on latency. If you want we can run a head-to-head on your real workloads.
[06:35] Jon: Let's do that — benchmark against OpenAI and Anthropic for our top 10 prompt families.
[06:39] Priya: Priya will own the benchmark and we'll include both latency and token cost metrics.

[06:44] Maya: On contract/commits — we are interested in a 12-month Dedicated reservation if the numbers look good. Who on Redwood handles that?
[06:51] Alex: I'll follow up with a formal proposal. Jordan will loop in sales ops for contract terms.
[06:57] Jordan: Yep I'll prepare sample SOW and reserved capacity terms.

[07:02] Alex: Alright last part — recap of action items and owners. Priya to run 2k token p95 benchmark and compare quantized vs non-quant; Alex to send pricing scenarios (3 utilization cases) and Dedicated cost model; Jordan to schedule security deep-dive and send SOC2 rotation docs; Maya to share masked staging corpus for eval. Anything to add?
[07:20] Maya: Could you also include an example of failover policy configuration in the Console?
[07:25] Priya: Yup we'll include a short runbook and a screenshot.

[07:29] Alex: Great. Thanks everyone for the time. We'll follow up in email with the sheets and schedule.
[07:35] Jon: Thanks, bye.
[07:36] Maya: Bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings — e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "KV cash" in earlier auto notes; speaker labels might have small inconsistencies.

End of transcript.
